candidate_relations.label: Acute respiratory failure
candidate_relations.reason: The benchmark reference requires identification of the causative infectious agent (Severe Influenza A H3N2). Acute respiratory failure describes the clinical syndrome resulting from the infection (evidenced by SpO2 86% on room air, increased respiratory rate, frothy sputum, bilateral infiltrates) but does not capture the etiologic diagnosis confirmed by PCR. It is a manifestation/complication rather than the final diagnostic object requested.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Acute respiratory failure is a complication/manifestation of the underlying Influenza A (H3N2) infection, not the primary etiologic diagnosis

case_quality_flags: PCR confirmation of Influenza A H3N2 from post-mortem tissue suggests fatal outcome; severity qualifier 'severe' is well-supported by clinical deterioration
Concurrent severe hypertension (200/120 mmHg) and fetal bradycardia suggest additional obstetric complications not captured in the reference diagnosis
